justification: Two changes that turned out to be one. A pure deletion of an unreachable surface, and the ledger enforcement that makes the deletion COUNT - without it the tracked number stayed at 270 and by the project's own rule the work was not done. Standard rather than Critical because nothing here chooses a regulatory value: the deletion removes a false claim, and every ledger change either wires an existing command or adds a read-only probe. Standard rather than Light because the deleted endpoint was live HTTP serving a table that contradicted the LEP in 135 places, and because dq_check.py is the merge gate itself - a mistake in it would either block every branch or, far worse, silently stop enforcing.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_dq_ratchet_enforcement.py -q; python scripts/dq_probe_zone_lint_keyed_map.py; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-73; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-74; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-41; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-33
falsifiable_check.fails_when: a ratchet cap rises above origin/main, or a row is newly declared fixed with no check, or DQ-41/DQ-33 regress, or DQ-73/74/75 stop being red while still unfixed
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Yes, each one, deliberately rather than by luck. Cap ratchet: set to 57 against main's 56 and watched it report the rise; 48 correctly did not. Newly-fixed rule: flipped DQ-66 from open to fixed with its check removed and watched it name DQ-66. The 18 enforcement tests were MUTATION-checked - stubbing raised_caps and newly_fixed_without_check to `return []` kills 5 of them, and the 13 that survive are the ones asserting emptiness, which must. DQ-75's probe exits 1 today and exits 0 under a patched check_line, so the row is closeable and not permanently red. DQ-73 and DQ-74 exit 1 as open rows must. DQ-41's zero was shown to be a measurement rather than a query that cannot match: widened to any first-of-month it returns 301.

pre_impl.existing_data: lep_land_use_table holds 18,196 rows across 26 LGAs, 32 zones and 356 development types, with permissibility in {permitted 9531, prohibited 8146, exempt 519}. It carries NO source_ref and NO effective_date column, so issue #928's suggested fix of returning both with each row is not implementable against the current schema. The deleted endpoint took no council parameter while the real table is keyed lga+zone.
pre_impl.reachability: Traced every caller before deleting. /api/development-types had exactly three references: contexts/DevelopmentContext.tsx (whose DevelopmentProvider is rendered by no page, only by its own test), store/slices/developmentSlice.ts (whose fetchDevelopmentTypes thunk is dispatched nowhere), and lib/health/migration-health-check.ts (which only pings the URL). components/development/* was imported only by those two files and one test. GroupedSetbackDisplay had no renderer, and was the sole consumer of components/compliance/DevelopmentTypeSelector. components/development-selector-enhanced.tsx had no importer. The whole redux store existed solely to hold the dead slice.
pre_impl.measured_defect: Compared the deleted ZONE_DEVELOPMENT_MAPPING against lep_land_use_table across 26 councils and the five hardcoded zones. 517 (council, zone, claim) triples evaluated: 289 agree, 135 contradict, 93 indeterminate. 8 contradictions are explicit prohibited rows needing no inference (Inner West R2 boarding_houses, Georges River E1 residential_flat_buildings and E1 multi_dwelling_housing, Fairfield R3 residential_flat_buildings and R3 shop_top_housing, Canada Bay R3 shop_top_housing, Waverley R3 shop_top_housing, Inner West R1 dual_occupancies). The remaining 127 rest on the Item-4 catch-all, which reads prohibited for 23 of 26 councils in R2.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two. First, issue #928 states the fix is to re-point the endpoint at lep_land_use_table returning source_ref and effective_date per row; those columns do not exist on that table (id, zone, zone_name, lga, development_type, permissibility, notes, created_at), so the suggested fix is not implementable as written. Second, the issue calls the endpoint live and consumed, listing three call sites. All three are real references but none is reachable: the context provider is rendered by no page, the redux thunk is dispatched nowhere, and the third is a health check that only pings the URL. I initially repeated the issue's framing that a user could see this, then traced the render path and found no page. The endpoint was serving wrong data to anyone calling it directly, not to a user journey.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new surface. This is deletion only. The capability the endpoint claimed to provide - which development types are permitted in a zone - already exists correctly elsewhere and is already sourced from lep_land_use_table: app/api/lep/permissibility/route.ts and app/api/permissibility/check/route.ts. That is precisely why this was two parallel implementations of one question, one sourced and one invented, and why removing the invented one leaves no gap.

functions.name: checkApiEndpoints
functions.input: no arguments; iterates a literal list of endpoint paths
functions.output: healthy when every listed endpoint responds ok. The deleted endpoint is removed from the list, so the health check no longer counts a 404 from a route that no longer exists as a failure.
functions.why_it_changed: leaving the path in the list would turn a deliberate deletion into a permanent unhealthy status
functions.if_none: If the path were left in the list, checkApiEndpoints would fetch a route that no longer exists, get a 404, and report the API subsystem permanently unhealthy - turning an intentional deletion into a standing false alarm. Removing the entry keeps the check meaningful for the three endpoints that remain.

values.value: 135 of 517 hardcoded (council, zone, claim) triples contradict the LEP; 8 of those are explicit prohibitions
values.if_missing: without it the deletion reads as tidying dead code, when it is removal of a live surface that returned regulatory answers contradicting the councils' own instruments

values.value: 0 rendered callers for the deleted endpoint and components

break_it.scenario: Something imports a deleted module after this merge.
break_it.what_happens: tsc and the Next.js build fail on an unresolved import. Not silent.
break_it.covered_by: npx tsc --noEmit and the CI build
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx tsc --noEmit  # unresolved import surfaces here; currently 8 pre-existing react-map-gl errors, baseline 677
break_it.mitigated: tsc runs in the pre-commit hook against an error-count baseline and in CI, so an unresolved import cannot reach main silently.

break_it.scenario: An external consumer calls GET /api/development-types after deletion.
break_it.what_happens: 404 instead of a 200 carrying wrong data. Loud rather than silent, and the previous behaviour was the harmful one. No first-party caller exists.
break_it.repro: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:3003/api/development-types?zone=R2  # expect 404 after this change, was 200 with wrong data
break_it.mitigated: Accepted deliberately, not mitigated. A 404 is the correct response for a route that should not exist, and it is louder than the previous behaviour of returning 200 with regulatory claims that contradict the LEP in 135 places. No first-party caller exists to break.
break_it.how: Not mitigated by a guard, accepted by design: the reachability trace in pre_impl shows zero first-party callers, and a 404 is a louder failure than the 200-with-wrong-data it replaces.

break_it.how: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest — 83 suites / 1,110 tests pass after deletion, plus the grep in this scenario's repro returning zero hits outside the deleted test.

break_it.scenario: A copy of the same hardcoded table survives elsewhere and keeps serving.
break_it.what_happens: two further copies of ZONE_DEVELOPMENT_TYPES existed and are deleted here. A third copy remains under migratePRPs/backup/ui_swap_20250921_213550/, which is an explicit backup directory, is imported by nothing, and is left untouched as pre-existing dead code.
break_it.covered_by: grep for ZONE_DEVELOPMENT_TYPES tree-wide, recorded in residual_risk
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && grep -rn 'ZONE_DEVELOPMENT_TYPES\|ZONE_DEVELOPMENT_MAPPING' --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx . | grep -v node_modules  # expect hits only under migratePRPs/backup/
break_it.mitigated: Partially mitigated. The two live copies are deleted here and lint_hardcoded_zone_codes.py guards against new ones. The surviving copy under migratePRPs/backup/ is imported by nothing and is left as pre-existing dead code; it still counts toward the zone-code baseline, which is recorded in residual_risk rather than silently cleaned.
break_it.how: python scripts/lint_hardcoded_zone_codes.py --all against .claude/zone_code_baseline.json — per-file counts are shrink-only, so the two deleted copies cannot return and the surviving backup copy stays counted rather than forgotten.

mutation_analysis: The deletion half cannot be mutation-tested - restoring any deleted file leaves it unimported so no test fails, which is exactly why the cluster survived eleven months; its guard is the shrink-only zone baseline, now correctly lowered 270 -> 263. The enforcement half WAS mutation tested: both new pure functions stubbed to `return []`, 5 of 18 tests die. That split is the honest result - 13 survive because they assert that nothing is found, and a return-[] mutant satisfies them by construction. Full suites green after both halves: 5,331 python passed / 2 skipped, and 83 jest suites / 1,110 tests.
residual_risk: Four things left open on purpose. (1) DQ-75 is logged, not fixed: widening the lint to catch a key-per-line map would fire on switch statements, test fixtures and the DCP Part keys PART_KEY_RE already excuses, and a noisy lint gets suppressed - worse than the gap. Fixing it will RAISE the baseline, which is the guard finding what was always there. (2) 38 rows remain declared fixed with no check; practice 1d stops that pile growing but cannot drain it. (3) DQ-58 is the one open row with no check, and its stated reason was TESTED today and found correct - check_failures pairs with council_url, the document, while DQ-58 is about council_page_url, the human page, so a check built on it would have measured the wrong URL and passed. (4) 115 scripts in scripts/ are untracked because .gitignore excludes the directory wholesale; only this branch's new probe was rescued, the rest are pre-existing and out of scope. Also: @reduxjs/toolkit and react-redux are now unused by app code but left in package.json, since dependency removal needs a fresh npm ci to verify rather than a junctioned node_modules.
